subject: [PATCH 2/2] mm/mempolicy: stop copying the nodemask in the interleave paths

reviews.author: Rakie Kim
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that matching two reads of a changing nodemask does not guarantee a correct distribution, and agreed with the patch's approach to simplify by only bounds checking the walk.
reviews.raw_body:
Fair enough. Your example makes the point. The mask can change after
the sum as well, so matching the two reads does not get us a correct
distribution either. Keeping it simple sounds right to me.

Please feel free to add the following to this patch:
Reviewed-by: Rakie Kim <rakie.kim@sk.com>

Thanks for walking through it.

Rakie Kim

2026-09-07.patch_summary: This patch removes the unnecessary copying of a nodemask in interleave node selectors, which reduces memory usage and improves performance. The original copy was done to ensure consistency between the node count and the walk, but this is no longer necessary as bounds checking can be used instead. If an empty nodelist or weight is detected, the patch falls back to using numa_node_id(). This change affects several functions in the mm/mempolicy.c file, including weighted_interleave_nid() and interleave_nid(), which are used for allocating pages under a specific memory policy.
